key_insight: Neural networks can learn inexact alternating minimization steps, accelerating convex optimization with quadratic coupling while enabling bounds on the optimality gap.
engineering_relevance: Replacing costly inner solvers with learned approximations can reduce runtime for robust matrix completion and low-dose CT reconstruction.
method: Use neural networks to approximate alternating subproblem solutions.
Train greedily on per-iteration errors identified by a worst-case optimality-gap bound.
Combine the bound with PAC-Bayes analysis for a fixed-horizon, high-probability guarantee on the expected gap.
evidence_signal: On robust matrix completion and dictionary-regularized low-dose CT reconstruction, the authors report 5–13× speedups over an inexact first-order baseline at matched accuracy, reaching up to 30× after brief end-to-end fine-tuning.
watch_item: The guarantees require convexity, quadratic coupling, and quadratic growth; the reported speedups should not be assumed to transfer to other problem classes.
paper_title: Learning inexact alternating minimization for convex problems with quadratic coupling
